newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Tag Heuer prices shares at 245 Sfr, listing today.
newsitem.headline: Tag Heuer prices shares at 245 Sfr, listing today.

text.p: Swiss sports watch and chronograph maker TAG HEUER International SA said the price for its new shares had been set at 245 Swiss francs, at the top of the expecting pricing range.
TAG HEUER also said in a statement that the shares had been accepted for listing on the Swiss and New York Stock Exchanges.
The share offering raised around 613.7 million francs and the company's market capitalisation at the issue price is 1.3 billion, the company added.
Tag Heuer's initial public offering (IPO) was met with strong interest in the market and the company raised the size of the inital offering by around 36 percent.
The offering ultimately comprised 1,321,739 primary shares and 1,183,211 secondary shares owned by TAG Finances (180,870), management (160,000) and Doughty Hanson (842,341).
The underwriters were also granted an over-allotment option of 375,743 shares owned by TAG Finances (130,435 shares) and Doughty Hanson (842,341).
Assuming full exercise of the over-allotment option, around 53.5 percent of TAG Heuer's share capital will have been sold in the offering.
Salomon Brothers Inc and SBC Warburg are acting as joint global co-ordinators and book-runners of the flotation.
TAG Heuer's 1995 consolidated turnover rose to 379.6 million francs from 340 million in 1994. Its 1995 operating income rose 17 percent to 77 million francs.
It has also said that end-June results were up 10.5 percent from the end of June 1995.
TAG Heuer produces about 700,000 watches annually.
